custom redaction marker via --redact-marker flag","body":"## Motivation Right now the redaction marker is hardcoded к the string `***REDACTED***` in `secure_log2test/core/parser.py:38`. Some teams prefer different markers for compliance review or downstream log-shipping pipelines (`[REDACTED-BY-S2LT]`, `<>`, custom company prefix). A `--redact-marker` CLI flag lets users pick the marker without editing source. ## Acceptance criteria - New CLI flag `--redact-marker MARKER` (default keeps `***REDACTED***`) - The marker propagates from `main.py` argparse into `redact_headers` and `redact_body` in `core/parser.py` - Existing tests using the default marker continue to pass unchanged - New tests cover: (a) default marker preserved when flag absent, (b) custom marker like `[SCRUBBED]` applied to headers, (c) custom marker applied to body fields, (d) empty string marker raises `ValueError` from argparse with clear message - README `Usage` section gets one short example: `secure-log2test in.json --redact-marker "[SCRUBBED]"` ## Implementation hint The marker currently lives as a module-level constant `REDACTED` at `secure_log2test/core/parser.py:38`. Two options: 1. Pass marker as an argument through `redact_headers(headers, marker=REDACTED)` and `redact_body(body, marker=REDACTED)`, plus a class-level override on `KibanaLogEntry` 2. Use a context-var or `contextlib.ContextDecorator` to set the active marker per parse session Option 1 is more explicit and easier to test. Option 2 is shorter but adds hidden state. The acceptance tests assume option 1; please flag in the PR if you prefer option 2 and we can discuss. CLI wiring lives in `secure_log2test/cli.py` (search for `argparse.ArgumentParser`). ## Test pattern ```python def test_custom_redact_marker_applied_to_headers(): cleaned = redact_headers( {"Authorization": "Bearer x"}, marker="[SCRUBBED]", ) assert cleaned["Authorization"] == "[SCRUBBED]" def test_custom_redact_marker_applied_to_body(): cleaned = redact_body( {"password": "secret"}, marker="[SCRUBBED]", ) assert cleaned["password"] == "[SCRUBBED]" def test_default_marker_preserved_when_flag_absent(): cleaned = redact_headers({"Authorization": "Bearer x"}) assert cleaned["Authorization"] == REDACTED def test_empty_marker_rejected_by_argparse(capsys): with pytest.raises(SystemExit): cli.main(["sample.json", "--redact-marker", ""]) ``` ## Out of scope - Per-header / per-body custom markers (single marker per run is enough for v1) - Marker templating with placeholders like `[REDACTED-{header_name}]` (open a separate issue if anyone needs it) - Encrypting redacted values (different feature, separate issue) Use a context-var or `contextlib.ContextDecorator` to set the active marker per parse session Option 1 is more explicit and easier to test. Option 2 is shorter but adds hidden state.
